notes: Amex IDaaS gateway; one pcm16_24k clip per request; text output.
Up to 30 clips evaluated concurrently; local models remain sequential.
The same reference baseline prompts and dataset-specific candidate labels as local audio LLMs.
Unparseable answers after retries are invalid, not an additional prompted emotion.
Answers become one-hot vectors, not calibrated class probabilities.
Raw answers and token usage are checkpointed in /Users/lchen65/Github/Fraud_Audio_Project/emotion_recognition/emotion_recognition_benchmarking/outputs/gpt_realtime/responses.jsonl.
Realtime has no enforced output schema; answers can vary between runs.
Allowed answers: angry, happy, neutral, sad, surprised; prompt 810c234fb672.

columns.audio_path: audio file, relative to the emotion_recognition/ folder
columns.acted_emotion: ground truth: the emotion each speaker was asked to portray, from the second part of the file name
columns.prediction: model prediction: the most probable of the 5 emotions evaluated (angry, happy, neutral, sad, surprised)
columns.prediction_all_classes: model prediction: the most probable of all 8 model classes
columns.correct: whether prediction equals acted_emotion or is accepted for it (excited: happy or surprised)
columns.p_*: model probability of each of its 8 classes (they add up to 1)
